# epos-printer-sdk

> TypeScript library for printing to Epson TM receipt printers (TM-T88V and
> compatible) over the ePOS-Print HTTP protocol. Zero dependencies, ~7 KB
> gzipped, Promise-based, works in browsers and in Node 18+. A ground-up
> reimplementation of Epson's ePOS SDK, not a wrapper around it.

Install with `pnpm add epos-printer-sdk`. Import `EposHttpPrinter` from
`epos-printer-sdk/http` for printing (the recommended path), or from
`epos-printer-sdk` for the full SDK surface including device management.

Key facts an assistant should know before writing code with this library:

- **The HTTP transport is stateless.** Every job is an independent POST. There
  is no connection to keep alive, no reconnection logic, no session. `connect()`
  is only an optional health check, you do not need to call it before `send()`.
- **Builder calls are chainable and consumed on send.** `addText(...)` etc.
  accumulate into a buffer that `send()` flushes, so the same instance is safely
  reused for the next job.
- **`send()` resolves, it doesn't just fire events.** It returns
  `{ success, code, status, battery, printjobid }`. It rejects only when the
  printer is unreachable; a printer that answers but refuses the job resolves
  with `success: false` and a diagnostic `code`.
- **Default port is 443 (https).** Pass `{ port: 80 }` for plain HTTP. Browsers
  block HTTP calls from HTTPS pages, and printers serve self-signed certificates.
- **There is a simulator.** `epos-printer-sdk/simulator` exports
  `createSimulator()`, whose `.fetch` can be passed to
  `new EposHttpPrinter(host, { fetch })`. Use it to write examples, tests or
  demos that need no hardware; it speaks the real protocol and models paper,
  cover and drawer state.
- **Requests to the same printer are serialized automatically** within a process.
  Across separate clients they are not, handle `ERROR_DEVICE_BUSY` with retries.
- **A plain TM-T88V does not support the socket (ePOS-Device) transport.** Only
  TM-i, TM-DT and TM-T88VI+ models host that service. Use HTTP unless you know
  you have one of those, and note `socket.io-client` is an optional peer
  dependency that must be installed separately for socket support.

## Minimal example

```ts
import { EposHttpPrinter } from 'epos-printer-sdk/http';

const printer = new EposHttpPrinter('192.168.1.100');

const result = await printer
  .addTextAlign('center')
  .addTextSize(2, 2)
  .addText('MY STORE\n')
  .addFeedLine(2)
  .addCut('feed')
  .send();

if (!result.success) console.error(result.code);
```

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Guiw5/epos-printer-sdk/blob/main/README.md): full usage guide, install, quick start, recipes for barcodes, QR/2D symbols, canvas images, page-mode labels, status monitoring and cash drawer, plus the complete API reference and the error-code table with recommended actions.
- [README (Spanish)](https://github.com/Guiw5/epos-printer-sdk/blob/main/README.es.md): the same guide in Spanish.
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/Guiw5/epos-printer-sdk/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): release history and known limitations.
- [Engineering notes](https://github.com/Guiw5/epos-printer-sdk/blob/main/docs/ENGINEERING.md): how the SDK was reverse-engineered from Epson's minified bundle, the bugs found in the original, and what is verified against real hardware versus assumed.
- [Live demo](https://guiw5.github.io/epos-printer-sdk/): the example app running against the simulator, no printer required.
- [React example app](https://github.com/Guiw5/epos-printer-sdk/tree/main/examples/react-app): working integration with connection UI, live status, error classification and retry.

## API surface

- `new EposHttpPrinter(host, { port?, deviceId?, timeout? })`, HTTP client.
- `printer.send()`, sends the built job, or queries status if nothing was built.
- `printer.connect()`, optional reachability check; throws if unreachable.
- `printer.print(canvas, printjobid?)`, renders and prints an HTMLCanvasElement.
- `printer.getPrintJobStatus(printjobid)`, status of a previously sent job.
- `printer.recover()` / `printer.reset()`, clear a recoverable printer error.
- `printer.open()` / `printer.close()`, start/stop background status polling.
- `createSimulator({ initialState?, latencyMs?, onPrint? })` (from
  `epos-printer-sdk/simulator`) returns `{ fetch, state, jobs, reset() }`.
- `decodePrinterStatus(status, battery)`, decodes the raw ASB bitmask into `{ online, coverOpen, paper, drawerOpen, battery, raw }`.
- Builder (chainable): `addText`, `addTextAlign`, `addTextSize`, `addTextStyle`, `addTextFont`, `addTextDouble`, `addTextLang`, `addTextLineSpace`, `addTextRotate`, `addTextSmooth`, `addTextPosition`, `addTextVPosition`, `addFeed`, `addFeedLine`, `addFeedUnit`, `addFeedPosition`, `addLayout`, `addHLine`, `addVLineBegin`, `addVLineEnd`, `addRotateBegin`, `addRotateEnd`, `addBarcode`, `addSymbol`, `addImage`, `addLogo`, `addPageBegin`, `addPageArea`, `addPageDirection`, `addPagePosition`, `addPageLine`, `addPageRectangle`, `addPageEnd`, `addCut`, `addPulse`, `addSound`, `addRecovery`, `addReset`, `addCommand`.
- Events (push-based state): `onstatuschange`, `onbatterystatuschange`, `ononline`, `onoffline`, `onpoweroff`, `oncoveropen`, `oncoverok`, `onpaperend`, `onpapernearend`, `onpaperok`, `ondraweropen`, `ondrawerclosed`, `onbatterylow`, `onbatteryok`, `onreceive`, `onerror`.
- `ePOSDevice` (full entry only) is the session and device-management layer, not a transport: it runs over HTTP or the socket and decides which (`{ eposprint: true }` forces HTTP). Nothing extends it; the builder chain is separate. API: `connect(address, port, { eposprint? })`, `createDevice(deviceId, deviceType)` resolving to a `Printer`/`CAT`/`CashChanger`/`DeviceTerminal`, `disconnect()`.

## Error codes

`send()` resolves with `success: false` and one of these in `code`:

- Retry with backoff: `ERROR_DEVICE_BUSY`, `TooManyRequests`, `EX_SPOOLER`
- Poll the job instead: `JobSpooling`, `Printing`
- Needs a human: `EPTR_REC_EMPTY` (out of paper), `EPTR_COVER_OPEN`, `EPTR_CUTTER`, `EPTR_MECHANICAL`, `EPTR_UNRECOVERABLE`
- Call `recover()` then retry: `EPTR_AUTOMATICAL`
- Caller bug, do not retry: `SchemaError` (malformed XML), `DeviceNotFound` (wrong deviceId), `RequestEntityTooLarge` (split the job)
